sentences.text: Two valid species of Dinornis are the North Island giant moa and the South Island giant moa.
Dinornis had reddish-brown, hair-like feathers covering most of its body.
Dinornis had large, powerful feet capable of delivering a strong kick when threatened.
Dinornis had large, powerful feet and a long neck that allowed it to reach high vegetation.
Female Dinornis may have been the tallest bird ever, reaching approximately 3.6 meters in height.
Female Dinornis are estimated to have weighed between 230 and 278 kilograms.
Dinornis eggs were enormous, roughly the size of a rugby ball and 80 times the volume of a chicken egg.
The genus Dinornis was described by Richard Owen in 1843.
Dinornis had long necks and broad, sharp beaks adapted for eating vegetation from subalpine herbs to tree branches.
Male Dinornis likely incubated eggs for up to three months before hatching.
Giant moa chicks were able to see, run, and feed themselves immediately after hatching.
Dinornis fossils date from the Late Pleistocene to the Holocene.
All species of Dinornis went extinct by the year 1500.
Dinornis was endemic to New Zealand.
Before humans arrived, Dinornis maintained a stable population in New Zealand for at least 40,000 years.
Dinornis was wiped out by Polynesian settlers who hunted them for food.
Māori are known to have hunted Dinornis by driving them into holes and stealing their nests.
The time range for Dinornis is from 0.129 million years ago to the present (Holocene).
